title: SR2021 No10 2026 wastewater-sludge anaerobic-digestion emissions QA controls

sources.title: SR2021 No 10: anaerobic digestion of non-hazardous sludge at a waste water treatment works, including the use of the resultant biogas

facts.source_fact: SR2021 No10 is for anaerobic digestion of non-hazardous sludge at a waste water treatment works including use of resultant biogas.
The permit is for a Part A installation with biological treatment capacity exceeding 100 tonnes per day.
The annual acceptance limit is no more than 500,000 tonnes.
The rules apply to England.
The rules and generic risk assessment were updated on 26 February 2026.
The 2026 update changed Activity 4 for treating biogas and biomethane.
Captured, treated and stored carbon dioxide requirements were added in the 2026 update.
The generic risk assessment added accidental release of carbon dioxide.
CCR/HCR statements require a site-specific decarbonisation readiness report.
The readiness report must be reviewed and updated at intervals not exceeding 2 years.
Point-source emissions to air, water or land are prohibited except from listed sources and emission points.
Point-source emissions must be identified on a site plan.
Periodic monitoring is required at least every 5 years for groundwater and 10 years for soil unless based on systematic contamination-risk appraisal.
Biogas combustion stacks are subject to annual periodic monitoring over a minimum one-hour reference period.
Monitoring uses MCERTS certification or accreditation where available unless otherwise agreed by the Environment Agency.
The listed NOx limit is 500 mg/m3 using EN 14792.
The listed carbon monoxide limit is 1400 mg/m3 using EN 15058.
The rules distinguish existing combustion plant sulphur dioxide limits before 2030 from the lower limit from 1 January 2030.
The listed total VOC limit including methane is 1000 mg/m3 using EN 12619.
The generic risk assessment includes diffuse greenhouse and polluting gas risks such as methane and ammonia.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the cited wastewater-sludge rule fact.
Attach the 2026 rule version and transition dates.
Carry emission point, method, standard and frequency provenance.
Do not convert facility permit requirements to parcel measurements.
